findings.label: Eight literature signals (short-term reversal, MAX/lottery, price-to-52-week-high, betting-against-beta, Amihud illiquidity, volume-shock-on-flat-price, close-at-day's-extreme, turn-of-month)
findings.claim: Any of eight documented cross-sectional or calendar anomalies beats a random-day baseline out-of-sample
findings.detail: Pre-registered before any data was fetched (protocol fixed in advance: next_open as the ONLY entry timing, hold_days and block lengths chosen from each signal's own literature horizon, direction predictions and the Bonferroni denominator all written down first -- closing the pre-registration gap that keeps the credit-spread anomaly un-elevated). 8 signals x 2 directions = 16 cells under one shared n_tests=16 threshold of 0.003125. Result: 0 of 16 confirmation-period primary cells significant. Two side-findings worth keeping: MAX came out BACKWARDS (high-MAX leg +3.32%/month, p=0.070; long-short spread -3.72% against the literature's sign) -- consistent with a 2019-2026 semiconductor/tech-heavy universe rewarding high-volatility names, an artifact of this universe rather than a refutation of the anomaly; and turn-of-month failed its own built-in placebo (the mid-month control leg, -0.367%, was MORE negative than the turn-of-month leg, -0.198%), so there is nothing there before significance is even considered. CRITICAL CAVEAT ON THE FIVE MONTHLY SIGNALS: this test could not have detected the effect it was looking for. Minimum detectable effect at the 0.003125 bar was 1.6-5.7% per month against the ~0.5-1%/month these anomalies actually claim -- 3x to 11x too coarse. Working back from the observed ~7.9% monthly dispersion, resolving a 0.5%/month effect would need ~2185 monthly observations (~180 years); even at an uncorrected alpha=0.05 it needs ~80 years. For signals 1-5 the honest verdict is UNTESTABLE ON THIS DATA, which is a different claim from rejected. The obvious fix was tested and REFUTED: testing the long-short spread instead of each leg separately INCREASES the standard error (0.59-0.97x), because edge_vs_own_ticker_pct already removes each ticker's own drift, so differencing two weakly-correlated 10-name estimates just adds variance. The binding constraint is 32 confirmation months x 10 names per leg, not the estimator. The two daily signals (349-468 confirmation dates) are far better positioned and their rejections carry real weight.

findings.label: Cross-asset macro signals (VIX spike, credit spread, yield curve)
findings.detail: 0/2 confirmation-period primary cells significant for all three signals under same_close (unrealistic) entry timing. Credit spread's 'up' leg looked strongly significant in discovery (p<0.001) but flipped to a small non-significant edge in confirmation. Re-checked 2026-07-26 under realistic next_open entry timing: VIX and yield curve unchanged (still rejected); credit spread's DIP leg flipped from non-significant (p=0.128) to significant (p=0.0, mean edge +1.39%) in confirmation. NOT elevated to confirmed/promising -- testing both timings without pre-registering which one counts is an uncorrected extra look (same multiple-testing risk this project's own by-block docstring warns about for weighting/block-length variants). Treat as an unconfirmed anomaly pending a dedicated, properly-scoped re-test (block-length sensitivity, trade_weighted comparison, and ideally a fresh discovery/confirmation split with next_open pre-registered as the only timing tested) before trusting it. THRESHOLD CORRECTION (2026-07-29): the script that produced the next_open re-check (scripts/run_execution_timing_revalidation.py) was passing the per-signal default n_tests=2 while scanning 5 signals x 2 entry timings x 2 directions = 20 cells in one pass, so its Bonferroni threshold was 0.025 when it should have been 0.05/20 = 0.0025 -- 10x too lenient, in the direction that manufactures false positives. Fixed (the denominator is now derived from the run list, pinned by tests/test_significance_multiplicity.py). This does NOT change the verdict here: the dip leg's confirmation p was below the 2000-resample bootstrap's resolution (reported 0.0, i.e. p<0.0005) and so clears the corrected threshold too, and no other recorded confirmation-period p-value falls in the affected [0.0025, 0.025] window. The anomaly therefore still stands exactly as described above -- unconfirmed, pending the dedicated re-test, and NOT elevated -- for the pre-registration reason already stated, not for a threshold reason. DOWNGRADED 2026-07-30 -- the evidence is now believed to be a measurement artifact, and the dedicated re-test is no longer worth running as specified. The entire case rested on 'p was below the 2000-resample bootstrap's resolution (reported 0.0)'. The block bootstrap was then calibrated directly against pure noise (true mean edge exactly zero) at this finding's own shape -- 31 signal dates, ~100 rows/date, primary block_length=10 -- and it returns exactly p=0.0 on 7% of pure-noise trials under an assumption-free i.i.d. null, and 15.5% under a persistent-common-factor null. Its false-positive rate at the 0.00833 threshold was 10% (12x nominal) and 18.5% respectively. So 'p=0.0 at 31 dates' is roughly what a coin-flip produces one run in seven, not evidence of an edge. Two structural causes, both now fixed in backtest/engine.py: longer blocks were MORE anti-conservative rather than less (12.5% -> 18.5% -> 29% across block lengths 5/10/15), and below ~50 signal dates no block length is calibrated at all (3.5-6.5x nominal), so bootstrap_edge_significance_by_block()/bootstrap_daily_edge_significance_by_block() now REFUSE to emit a p-value in that regime and return a refusal_reason instead. Re-running this signal today produces no p-value at all rather than p=0.0. NOTE THE DIRECTION: the defect made significance EASIER, never harder, so no REJECTED verdict anywhere in this registry is affected -- only positive results at small n_dates are, and this is the only one. A separate re-run on the 2026-07-30 snapshot also showed the YIELD CURVE 'up' leg reading p=0.003 against a 0.00833 threshold; that is likewise inside the uncalibrated regime (n_dates=28) and is a repeated look at an already-rejected hypothesis, so it was deliberately NOT recorded as a finding. See tests/test_block_bootstrap_calibration.py.

findings.claim: Improves risk-adjusted return over plain inverse-volatility targeting
findings.detail: Looked like a breakthrough on a single discovery/confirmation split but failed walk-forward validation. Structural flaw: the one-way ratchet can never re-lever once trimmed, so it structurally misses upside in an extended bull market. Kelly sizing itself (signed mean/variance) is a genuine improvement over inverse-vol targeting; the ratchet is the part that broke.

findings.label: Defensive-carry sleeve (TLT/IEF/SHY/GLD) blended into an equal-weight UNIVERSE portfolio
findings.claim: Reduces combined-portfolio drawdown/expected-shortfall vs. an equal-weight UNIVERSE baseline without giving up more upside than downside, relative to SPY
findings.detail: scripts/run_defensive_carry_probe.py, single 2019-07-22 to 2026-07-28 lookback window (1762-1763 sessions), no walk-forward or out-of-sample split yet. Carry-basket correlation to the UNIVERSE baseline was 0.041 and to SPY was 0.009 (near-zero, as expected for Treasuries/gold vs. equities); per-ticker vs SPY: TLT -0.121, IEF -0.078, SHY -0.009, GLD 0.134. The UNIVERSE-only baseline itself runs hot relative to SPY (downside_capture_pct 118.2, upside_capture_pct 120.8 -- this project's universe is semiconductor/tech-heavy). Blending in the carry basket monotonically reduced both max_drawdown_pct (-35.1% at 0% carry -> -26.7% at 30% carry) and expected_shortfall_pct_95 (-3.50% -> -2.70%) as the carry weight increased from 0% to 30%, while narrowing both capture ratios toward 100% (downside_capture_pct 118.2 -> 92.4%, upside_capture_pct 120.8 -> 95.1%). At the 30%-carry weight, downside capture (92.4%) was slightly BELOW upside capture (95.1%) -- a mildly asymmetric, favorable result on this single window -- but this is one lookback window with no significance testing, no walk-forward confirmation, and 3 candidate weights tested alongside the 0% baseline (a small multiple-comparisons surface). Not a recommendation and not a live/paper allocation change.
